children: Ascelia received FDA Type A minutes on Orviglance. FDA still requires added clinical evidence but may accept a prospective SPARKLE image reanalysis with a different primary endpoint. Ascelia will not run a new study and will pursue EU regulatory and partnering paths.
Extends U.S. approval timeline and raises regulatory risk.
Creates a potential non-trial path to approval, limiting costs and time.
Signals cash conservation and reliance on existing data; risk if FDA rejects.
Removes some CMC risk; issues tied to specs/procedures, not process.
Focus on EU regulatory and partnering
Shifts near-term catalysts to Europe and BD deals.

This is a mid-cycle regulatory update following an FDA CRL for Orviglance. A clear FDA agreement on an acceptable endpoint and a successful SPARKLE reanalysis would turn this into a major catalyst; EU regulatory milestones or a partnership deal could also move shares.
